questions.question: As a graph, what is Lesson 1's agent loop?
options: Two nodes (agent, tools) with a conditional edge from agent and a fixed edge back from tools
A straight line of five nodes
It can't be expressed as a graph
questions.explanation: agent -> tools if it requested tools, else END; tools -> agent. That's the whole loop.

questions.question: Why do nodes return partial updates merged by reducers, instead of the whole new state?
options: Each node only knows about what it changed, and reducers define how values combine (append messages, overwrite flags)
LangGraph requires it for no reason
questions.explanation: Partial updates keep nodes small and independent; reducers make merging explicit, which matters most when branches run in parallel.

questions.question: What does compile() catch before the graph runs?
options: Wiring mistakes: edges to unknown nodes, nodes without an outgoing edge, unreachable nodes
questions.explanation: Structural bugs fail at build time with a clear message instead of halfway through a paid run.

questions.question: Two parallel branches both lead to a 'join' node. In this lesson's runtime, how many times does join run in the next super-step?
options: Once: the active set is de-duplicated
questions.explanation: The next active set is a set of node names. Both branches' updates are already merged into the state join sees.

questions.question: The live run's check node passed an answer from memory because of the '2' in 'K2'. What's the general lesson?
options: Heuristic checkers have false positives too; test them against real outputs and keep each miss as a regression test
questions.explanation: Guards are code too, so they have bugs. Real model output is the best source of test cases for them.

questions.question: You need human approval before every tool call. In the graph, what's the smallest change?
options: compile(interrupt_before=('tools',)) and resume with resume_at=['tools'] after approval
Add approval text to the system prompt
questions.explanation: Interrupts are a runtime feature of the graph, so no node has to change.
